signature: SUBROUTINE ZGEES( JOBVS, SORT, SELECT, N, A, LDA, SDIM, W, VS,

params.name: jobvs
params.reference:
-   `= 'N'`: Schur vectors are not computed;
-   `= 'V'`: Schur vectors are computed.

params.name: sort
params.reference:
Specifies whether or not to order the eigenvalues on the diagonal of the Schur form.

-   `= 'N'`: Eigenvalues are not ordered:
-   `= 'S'`: Eigenvalues are ordered (see `SELECT`).

params.name: select
params.reference: `SELECT` must be declared EXTERNAL in the calling subroutine. If `SORT = 'S'`, `SELECT` is used to select eigenvalues to order to the top left of the Schur form. IF `SORT = 'N'`, `SELECT` is not referenced. The eigenvalue `W(j)` is selected if `SELECT(W(j))` is true.

params.name: N
params.reference: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the N-by-N matrix A. On exit, A has been overwritten by its Schur form T.
params.workDependent: the Schur form T is unique only up to unit phases, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A. $\mathrm{LDA} \ge \max (1,N)$.

params.name: sdim
params.reference:
If `SORT = 'N'`, `SDIM = 0`. If `SORT = 'S'`, `SDIM` = number of eigenvalues for which

`SELECT` is true.

params.name: w
params.reference: W contains the computed eigenvalues, in the same order that they appear on the diagonal of the output Schur form T.

params.name: VS
params.reference: If `JOBVS = 'V'`, `VS` contains the unitary matrix Z of Schur vectors. If `JOBVS = 'N'`, `VS` is not referenced.
params.workDependent: the Schur vectors are unique only up to the same unit phases as T, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change

params.name: ldvs
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array `VS`. $\mathrm{LDVS} \ge 1$; if `JOBVS = 'V'`, $\mathrm{LDVS} \ge N$.

params.name: WORK
params.reference: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

params.name: lwork
params.reference:
The dimension of the array `WORK`. $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge \max (1,2 \, N)$. For good performance, `LWORK` must generally be larger.

If `LWORK = -1`, then a workspace query is assumed; the routine only calculates the optimal size of the `WORK` array, returns this value as the first entry of the `WORK` array, and no error message related to `LWORK` is issued by XERBLA.

params.name: info
params.reference:
-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `> 0`: if `INFO = i`, and i is \<= N:  the QR algorithm failed to compute all the eigenvalues; elements 1:ILO-1 and i+1:N of W contain those eigenvalues which have converged; if `JOBVS = 'V'`, `VS` contains the matrix which reduces A to its partially converged Schur form. = N+1: the eigenvalues could not be reordered because some eigenvalues were too close to separate (the problem is very ill-conditioned); = N+2: after reordering, roundoff changed values of some complex eigenvalues so that leading eigenvalues in the Schur form no longer satisfy `SELECT` = .TRUE..  This could also be caused by underflow due to scaling.

untranslated: WORK.minLength: local MINWRK is assigned inside nested control flow

overrides.reason: ZGEES hands its LWORK to ZGEHRD, ZUNGHR and ZHSEQR, which pick their block size or AED window from LWORK. The blocked and unblocked Hessenberg reductions round differently, and the QR iteration that follows reaches a Schur form T that is unique only up to unit phases (and, past the reference's crossover, the eigenvalue order), with Schur vectors transformed to match. The reference does this as well: compiled LAPACK 3.12.0 ZGEES at N = 150 (random matrix, JOBVS = 'V') returns a different A, VS and order of W at LWORK = 2N than at its queried optimum. The JS zgehrd crosses over at NX = 32 where ILAENV(3) gives 128, so the JS path changes from N > 33 (the reference's from N > 128). The module's tests check the eigenvalues, SDIM and A = Z*T*Z^H at the minimum WORK past the blocking threshold (ticket 0100).

set.params.A.workDependent: the Schur form T is unique only up to unit phases, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change
set.params.VS.workDependent: the Schur vectors are unique only up to the same unit phases as T, which the LWORK-dependent Hessenberg blocking can change
